flow.workbookNotShared: This experiment's workbook is not shared with you.
flow.workbookNotSharedHint: Access is set per resource, so being added to the experiment does not include its workbook. Ask someone who can share the workbook to give you access.
flow.confirmDetachMessage: This will unlink the workbook from this experiment. The workbook and its versions won't be deleted, and existing measurement data is unaffected. The mobile app and data pipeline will continue to work with the current flow. You can re-attach a workbook later.
flow.confirmChangeMessage: Switching workbooks replaces this experiment's measurement protocol. Existing measurements and results are preserved, but all future measurements will follow the new workbook. Changing the flow mid-experiment can affect how comparable your data is.
flow.confirmUpgradeMessage: Upgrading pins this experiment to the latest workbook version, changing its measurement protocol for future measurements. Existing data is preserved, but changing the flow mid-experiment can affect how comparable your data is.

metadata.description: Attach custom metadata to your experiment data. Metadata columns are joined to each measurement row by a shared identifier and appear alongside sensor readings in the Data tab and exports on the next processing interval.
metadata.supportedFormats: Supports CSV, TSV, and Excel files (.xlsx, .xls)
metadata.pasteHint: Tip: You can also paste directly with {{shortcut}}
metadata.identifierHint: To choose the identifier column, open the ⋯ menu in its header and select "Set as identifier". Its values are matched against the match target below.

success.metadataDescription: Your metadata has been successfully saved to the experiment. It will be available in the Data tab and included in downloads.

studyDetails.title: Study details
studyDetails.organismHelp: The scientific name of what the study grows or observes.
studyDetails.experimentalDesignHelp: How plots, treatments and replicates are arranged, in a sentence or two.
studyDetails.experimentalDesignPlaceholder: e.g. Randomized blocks with three treatments and four replicates
studyDetails.growthFacilityHelp: Where the plants grew, such as an open field or a greenhouse.
studyDetails.licenseHelp: CC BY 4.0 lets anyone reuse the data if they credit the authors. CC0 1.0 gives the data to the public domain. New datasets start with this license, and a published dataset keeps the license it was published with.
studyDetails.dialogDescription: Say when the study ran, what it studied and how others may reuse the data. Exports and published datasets carry these facts, so fill in what you know.

layout.title: Layout
layout.description: The plots in this experiment, where each one sits, and what it is called.

firstRun.title: No plots yet

needsPlots.viewer: No plots yet. An experiment's admins and members lay out the plots.

walkingOrderEmpty.title: Walked in layout order
walkingOrderEmpty.description: Until a strategy is chosen, the app walks the plots in layout order, starting at {{first}}.

fieldDaysEmpty.title: No field days yet
fieldDaysEmpty.description: Each day's progress and any plots measured twice show here once a measurer starts a session in the app.

layout.levelNameHelp: What one unit is called, such as plot, tray or pot.

naming.label: Names
naming.range: The {{units}} are named {{first}} to {{last}}, row by row.

setup.description: Say what one unit is called and how the field is laid out. The grid shows what saving makes.
setup.removes_one: The new size leaves out {{count}} {{unit}}, {{measured}} of them measured. Saving asks you to confirm.
setup.removes_other: The new size leaves out {{count}} {{units}}, {{measured}} of them measured. Saving asks you to confirm.

preview.title: Preview
preview.description: What saving makes. Nothing is created until you save.

legend.specimenDescription: Every look a plot can take, the same on every grid.

gaps.banner: Click or drag over positions to turn {{units}} into gaps and gaps back into {{units}}.
gaps.confirmBody_one: {{names}} already has readings. It stays in the layout as Removed: its readings keep their {{unit}}, and it leaves the walking order and the plot picker.
gaps.confirmBody_other: {{names}} already have readings. They stay in the layout as Removed: their readings keep their {{units}}, and they leave the walking order and the plot picker.

unplaced.description_one: {{count}} {{unit}} has no row and column yet. Open it and choose Set position.
unplaced.description_other: {{count}} {{units}} have no row and column yet. Open one and choose Set position.

source.edit: From the sheet "{{sheet}}", edited after upload

term.label: Term
term.help: A greenhouse term (Common Greenhouse Ontology) tells an export what kind of unit this is. Most field plots have none.

anchor.title: Anchor on map
anchor.description: Say where the field is: the experiment location it belongs to, then two corners of the grid.
anchor.newLocation: Add a location from the map
anchor.locationHelp: The location alone already says where the experiment ran.
anchor.derived: Row A runs at {{bearing}}° from north, {{spacing}} m from one column to the next.
anchor.rowSpacingHelp: From the start of one row to the start of the next, paths included.
anchor.outlineHelpRight: The outline shows where the grid lies, with rows after A to the right of row A seen from the first plot. If they lie to the left, flip it. Even spacing is assumed, so a wider path between blocks shows as drift.
anchor.outlineHelpLeft: The outline shows where the grid lies, with rows after A to the left of row A seen from the first plot. Even spacing is assumed, so a wider path between blocks shows as drift.
anchor.partialHelp: Click the map to set the selected corner. With both corners and the row spacing, every plot gets coordinates.

sheetMatch.checking: Checking the sheet against the layout...
sheetMatch.duplicates: {{names}} appear more than once, and the first row of each wins.
sheetMatch.readings_one: {{count}} reading carries a {{level}} and shows these values once saved.
sheetMatch.readings_other: {{count}} readings carry a {{level}} and show these values once saved.
sheetMatch.noReadings: No reading carries a {{level}} yet. The values reach the Data tab once measurers name the {{level}} in the app.

plotQuestion.title: Which question names the {{unit}}?
plotQuestion.description: This experiment's workbook asks questions in the app. Pick the one measurers answer with the {{unit}}'s name, so the layout takes its place.
plotQuestion.after: The app shows its Next plot step in place of that question. Past answers keep matching sheets by question, and the data dictionary marks the column as described by the layout.

placement.title: Place on plot
placement.description: The sensor stands on the plot from the start date. Moving or removing it later ends the placement and keeps its history.
placement.sensorHelp: A reading that names this sensor carries its plot. A reading that names no sensor carries the plot of the whole device.
placement.startDateHelp: Readings taken from this date on carry the plot.
placement.overlap: {{sensor}} already stands on plot {{plot}} since {{date}}. Use Move on that placement, or choose another sensor.
placement.listDescription: Each reading carries the plot its sensor stood on when it was taken.

plotList.placed_other: {{count}} {{units}} placed on {{rows}} rows by {{columns}} columns, leaving {{gaps}} gaps.
